thread:
jamie: quick heads-up — synthetic replay showed a P99 tail jump after the latest runtime change. p95 ~ 42ms, p99 ~ 1.2s (baseline p99 ~ 0.9s).

michelle: oof. which change are we blaming? kernel selection or batching? :thinking:

jamie: initial profiler points at batching heuristic + KV cold misses interacting. looks like small QPS periods get forced into min_batch=8 which increases queueing when seq len variable. also seeing KV cache miss spike during spikes.

raj: do you have the load profile used for the replay? can you paste the schedule?

jamie: here — this is the loadgen config I used (shortened):
```
load_profile:
  schedule:
    - duration_s: 30
      target_qps: 5
    - duration_s: 120
      target_qps: 250
      burst_qps: 900
    - duration_s: 300
      target_qps: 60
  tail_shaping: pareto(alpha=1.3)
batching:
  min_batch: 8
  max_window_ms: 7
kv_cache:
  prewarm_pct: 0
  ttl_s: 300
```

jamie: note the long-tail shaping is explicit (pareto) so we inject >1% heavy requests which exercise KV misses and non-amortized kernel selection.

michelle: got it. can you also paste profiler snippet? e.g., top stacks?

jamie: pasted short output:
```
samples  function
  34%   runtime::batcher::wait_for_batch
  18%   runtime::kv::populate_cache
  12%   runtime::kernel_selector::select
  8%    runtime::executor::emit_tokens
```

sumi: the `min_batch: 8` is the interesting bit. at low QPS that creates artificial latency because we wait window_ms to fill. we had a change to prefer larger batches to improve throughput for steady high QPS — but we didn't make it adaptive based on QPS.

raj: agree. two axes to try: adaptive min_batch (based on observed qps/sec) and a KV prewarm phase for burst windows. maybe also allow immediate fallback to single-instance kernel if waiting > X ms.

perf-bot: regression alert: p99 increased 12% on eng-runtime/stable after deploy 1798870000. Suspected components: batching heuristic, kv-cache. Links: https://perf/reports/17988

michelle: can we do apples-to-apples? replay harness should be identical binary + seed + kv state. jamie — did you reset KV snapshot before replay?

jamie: i did not — that was the mistake. replay used a cold KV (prewarm_pct:0). rerunning with prewarm_pct:80 now. will re-run with identical binary and same seed.

jamie: new run (in progress) shows p99 back to ~0.95s when prewarmed and adaptive batch patch applied locally. still validating.

raj: propose follow-ups: 1) make batcher adaptive heuristic (patch ready to review) 2) add prewarm stage to synthetic orchestration (config toggle) 3) e2e apples-to-apples checklist for perf runs (binary+seed+kv snapshot).

michelle: ^+1. open a GH issue for the checklist and another for the batcher change. tag @eng-runtime on both.

jamie: opened GH #4221 (batcher adaptive) and #4222 (perf-run checklist + kv snapshot). I added notes about QPS schedule and pareto tail parameters.

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for batcher-adaptive branch to perf cluster (depends on #4221).

sumi: nice. after canary we should run the long-tail shaped replay (pareto alpha sweep 1.1–1.5) and record p50/p95/p99 and KV miss rates. add a small script to the harness to automate alpha sweep.

jamie: will add sweep script to loadgen and post results here. thanks everyone. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
